utterances.text: Well, the look of this room, the kind of table, and if you compare these photographs, you see this is one and the same person, only taken from different angles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, where did you meet this person whom -- who is, as you say, called Fuad Kaknjo?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I met Mr. Fuad Kaknjo sometime in mid-1992 when he was the president of the local government in the Municipality of Vitez. That is when I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with him at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you also mentioned that you still had contact with him?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are working in the same building, in the same place. He is with the ministry for reconstruction and development. I think he's deputy minister or assistant minister. He is an engineer. I don't know his speciality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you meet him often?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Daily, because we work in the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might you be wrong about him? You are sure this is not a case of mistaken identity?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. After this colour photograph I am positive that it is him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, would you know, when you talked to Mr. Kaknjo, do you know -- are you aware that he was in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: I heard that he was in Kaonik, that is, I heard it from other persons, because he is not an unfamiliar face in the Territorial Municipality of Vitez and around it. So I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he speak to you about it personally?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if -- do you know when it was that he was in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Well, this is difficult to say, but it must have been in the early -- in late April or early May, during those events, and I heard from some close friends of his that it was at that time the end of April '93. But I wouldn't know when he went there, how long he spent there, when he came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, at that time did you have an opportunity to visit Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Because military operations were underway in the Municipality of Vitez, and the Municipality of Vitez is midway between the Municipality of Travnik and Busovaca, so that during that time period the road was closed, naturally, by the military police, and for safety reasons they did not allow one to go across the territory of the Municipality of Vitez. And that was the only road taking one to the Kaonik Prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, when you look at this photograph you see several persons on it. Will you please pay attention to the person in the middle, in the second -- on the right-hand side of the photograph. That person's finger is -- thumb is bandaged. You see that this person has around his neck a piece of jewellery or something? What could it be?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Well, it could be a chain. What else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, do you see, if you look at Mr. Kaknjo in the left-hand upper corner of this photograph, if he has any bruises, any injuries on his face?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Well, one doesn't see them on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please remove this photograph from the ELMO, because we shall not need it any more. And, Your Honours, I should like these two documents to be admitted into evidence, only the photographs, not the text. Only photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Mikulicic. Can the registrar please give us the number for this particular document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last document shall give the reference D/24. And as for documents D/22A and B, I do not believe that it was requested that these be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Are you requesting that it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. I see there is no objection. Therefore, they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Percinlic, when you next went to -- had an opportunity to go to Kaonik, when was that?

utterances.speaker: ZELKO PERCINLIC
utterances.text: Well, it was only in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not pursue that, because it's not during the relevant times. Mr. Percinlic, this would therefore conclude my examination, and the Defence has no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to make an application for an adjournment until tomorrow, before I conduct my cross-examination of this witness. There are several matters in the transcript that I really need to check very carefully before I conduct my cross-examination, and I would be most grateful if the Court could indulge me with that time in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, do you have any comments, an objection to what has been suggested?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence has nothing against this objection by the Prosecutor. We believe that the Prosecutor is entitled to have enough time for preparation. We would have preferred to finish today, but we do not have any objections to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, we shall grant this adjournment so that the Prosecution may examine all of these documents. I wonder if we can begin tomorrow? I believe then we're going to end this session at the moment where we would have begun with cross-examination, is that not right, Mr. Niemann and Mr. Mikulcic? Very well, in that case, we can begin at 9.30. Is that all right with you, Mr. Mikulcic? We shall begin at 9.30, is that all right with the interpreters? They also are in agreement with this, therefore we shall resume with this session tomorrow morning at 9.30. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
